definition: A special type of court order used in divorce proceedings that divides retirement plan benefits between divorcing spouses in a way that complies with ERISA. A QDRO creates or recognizes the right of a spouse to receive a portion of the other spouse's retirement plan benefits and must meet specific federal requirements to be valid.
examples: A QDRO issued in the Marschner divorce would need to comply with federal ERISA requirements for the retirement account division to be legally effective.
